p: 台風が来て、昨日は<ruby>沖縄<rt>おきなわ</rt></ruby>では大雨だった（　）。
en: I heard that because of the typhoon, it rained heavily in Okinawa yesterday.
np: आँधी आएर हिजो ओकिनावामा ठूलो वर्षा भएको थियो रे।
why: Sentence-final とか reports uncertain hearsay: “I heard that...” or “apparently...”.
wrong: のは makes the preceding clause a topic and needs a following predicate. とを is not a valid particle combination here. のを makes the clause an object and needs a following verb.
v: 台風（たいふう）= typhoon / आँधी; 来る（くる）= come / आउनु; 昨日（きのう）= yesterday / हिजो; 沖縄（おきなわ）= Okinawa / ओकिनावा; 大雨（おおあめ）= heavy rain / ठूलो वर्षा
g: Sentence-final ～とか means “I heard that...” or “apparently...”.

p:
妻「あなたの体のために、明日からたばこを吸うのをやめてちょうだい。」
夫「（　）厳しいことを言わないでよ。」
en: Wife: “For your health, please stop smoking from tomorrow.” Husband: “Don’t say something so strict.”
np: श्रीमती: “स्वास्थ्यका लागि भोलिदेखि चुरोट छोड्नुहोस्।” श्रीमान्: “त्यति कडा कुरा नगर न।”
why: そんなに means “that much/so” and refers naturally to the strict request the wife has just made.
wrong: こんなに refers to something close to the speaker. あんなに refers to something distant or previously observed. どんなに means “no matter how much” and normally combines with ～ても or ～か.
v: 妻（つま）= wife / श्रीमती; 夫（おっと）= husband / श्रीमान्; 体（からだ）= body, health / शरीर, स्वास्थ्य; 明日（あした）= tomorrow / भोलि; 吸う（すう）= smoke / धूम्रपान गर्नु; 厳しい（きびしい）= strict / कडा
g: Vるのをやめる means “stop doing V.” Vてちょうだい is an informal request, and Vないで asks someone not to do something.

p: 私は昨日から<ruby>風邪<rt>かぜ</rt></ruby>（　）で、熱が少しある。
en: I have felt slightly sick with a cold since yesterday and have a mild fever.
np: हिजोदेखि मलाई अलिअलि रुघा लागेको छ र थोरै ज्वरो पनि छ।
why: 風邪気味 means showing slight signs of a cold. 気味 behaves like a noun here, so 気味で connects correctly to the next clause.
wrong: 風邪っぽい is possible by itself, but before this で it would need to be 風邪っぽくて. ほど expresses degree. ～げ normally attaches to adjective stems, such as 悲しげ.
v: 私（わたし）= I / म; 昨日（きのう）= yesterday / हिजो; 風邪（かぜ）= cold / रुघा; 気味（ぎみ）= slight tendency / हल्का लक्षण; 熱（ねつ）= fever / ज्वरो; 少し（すこし）= a little / थोरै
g: N／Vます-stem＋気味（ぎみ） means “slightly...” or “showing a tendency toward...,” often for an undesirable condition.

p: 近所へ散歩に行った（　）、スーパーで牛乳を買ってきました。
en: While I was out taking a walk nearby, I also bought some milk at the supermarket.
np: नजिकै घुम्न गएको मौकामा सुपरमार्केटबाट दूध पनि किनेर ल्याएँ।
why: Vたついでに means doing an additional task while already doing something else.
wrong: かたがた is formal and normally follows a noun or verb stem, not 行った. かわりに means “instead of/in exchange for.” ままに means “as it is/as directed.”
v: 近所（きんじょ）= neighborhood / छिमेक; 散歩（さんぽ）= walk / घुमफिर; 牛乳（ぎゅうにゅう）= milk / दूध; 買ってくる（かってくる）= buy and bring back / किनेर ल्याउनु
g: Vた＋ついでに means “while doing that, take the opportunity to do something else.”

p: 学校から家へ帰る（　）彼女に会ったので、道で少し話しました。
en: I met her on the way home from school, so we talked briefly on the road.
np: विद्यालयबाट घर फर्किने बाटोमा उनीसँग भेट भएकाले केहीबेर कुरा गर्‍यौँ।
why: Vる途中で means “while in the middle of doing V” or “on the way.”
wrong: 途中まで means “up to the middle point.” 途中へ means “toward the middle” and cannot connect the event. 途中から means “from midway.”
v: 学校（がっこう）= school / विद्यालय; 家（いえ）= home / घर; 帰る（かえる）= return / फर्कनु; 途中（とちゅう）= on the way / बाटोमा; 彼女（かのじょ）= she / उनी; 会う（あう）= meet / भेट्नु; 道（みち）= road / बाटो
g: Vる途中（とちゅう）で indicates that another event occurs while the first action is in progress.

p: この町は、駅を（　）発展してきた。
en: This town has developed around the station.
np: यो सहर स्टेशनलाई केन्द्र बनाएर विकास हुँदै आएको हो।
why: Nを中心として means “with N as the center” or “centered around N.”
wrong: 中心とともに means “together with the center.” 中心において means “at the center” and cannot follow 駅を. 中心にかけて describes a range or direction.
v: 町（まち）= town / सहर; 駅（えき）= station / स्टेशन; 中心（ちゅうしん）= center / केन्द्र; 発展する（はってんする）= develop / विकास हुनु
g: Nを中心（ちゅうしん）として means “centered around N.” Vてくる describes a change continuing up to the present.

p: 毎朝私は、ベランダの花に水を（　）。
en: I water the flowers on the balcony every morning.
np: म हरेक बिहान बाल्कोनीका फूलमा पानी हाल्छु।
why: やる is used when giving something to plants or animals. 水をやる is the standard expression for watering plants.
wrong: くれる means someone gives to the speaker. もらう means to receive. さしあげる is a humble form used when giving to a respected person, not to flowers.
v: 毎朝（まいあさ）= every morning / हरेक बिहान; 私（わたし）= I / म; 花（はな）= flower / फूल; 水（みず）= water / पानी; やる = give to a plant or animal / दिनु, पानी हाल्नु
g: Japanese giving verbs change according to the relationship between giver and receiver. やる is natural for plants and animals.

p: 彼女に会うのは、卒業以来3年（　）。
en: This is the first time in three years that I have met her since graduation.
np: स्नातक भएपछि तीन वर्षमा पहिलो पटक उनीसँग भेट भएको हो।
why: A period＋ぶり means doing something for the first time after that length of time.
wrong: よりだ expresses comparison. ながらだ means “while/although.” からだ means “because” or “from,” not an interval since the previous occurrence.
v: 彼女（かのじょ）= she / उनी; 会う（あう）= meet / भेट्नु; 卒業（そつぎょう）= graduation / स्नातक; 以来（いらい）= since / देखि; 3年ぶり（さんねんぶり）= for the first time in three years / तीन वर्षपछि पहिलो पटक
g: N以来（いらい） means “since N.” Period＋ぶり means “for the first time after that period.”

o: お話しなさいましたか
en: What did your younger brother say to the teacher?
why: 申す is the humble form of 言う. The younger brother is treated as an in-group member and is lowered in relation to the teacher.
wrong: お話しなさいましたか, 話されましたか, and おっしゃいましたか are honorific expressions that raise the younger brother, so they are inappropriate here.
v: 弟（おとうと）= younger brother / भाइ; 先生（せんせい）= teacher / शिक्षक; 何と（なんと）= what / के भनेर; 言う（いう）= say / भन्नु; 申す（もうす）= say, humble / विनम्र रूपमा भन्नु
g: 申す（もうす） is 謙譲語（けんじょうご）, while おっしゃる is 尊敬語（そんけいご）.

p: あの子は、小さい子ども（　）、とてもかしこい。
en: That child is very clever for such a young child.
np: त्यो बच्चा सानो बच्चाको हिसाबले निकै बुद्धिमान छ।
why: Nにしては means “considering that someone is N” and introduces a result different from the usual expectation.
wrong: のあまり means “because of too much...”. であるからには means “now that/since it is the case.” からして means “judging from” or “starting with.”
v: 子ども（こども）= child / बच्चा; 小さい（ちいさい）= small, young / सानो; かしこい = clever / बुद्धिमान
g: Nにしては means “for an N/considering N,” usually followed by a surprising result.

p:
男の学生「あ、ペンを忘れちゃった。」
女の学生「私（　）、これを使ってよ。」
en: Male student: “Oh, I forgot my pen.” Female student: “If mine is okay, use this.”
np: छात्र: “मैले कलम बिर्सिएछु।” छात्रा: “मेरो भए हुन्छ भने, यो प्रयोग गर।”
why: 私のでよければ means “if mine is okay.” の replaces the already understood noun ペン, and でよければ means “if it is acceptable.”
wrong: のもよければ unnecessarily adds “also.” 私がよいから means “because I am good.” 私でよいから means “because I am acceptable”; both refer to the person rather than the pen.
v: 男の学生（おとこのがくせい）= male student / छात्र; 女の学生（おんなのがくせい）= female student / छात्रा; 忘れる（わすれる）= forget / बिर्सनु; 私の（わたしの）= mine / मेरो; 使う（つかう）= use / प्रयोग गर्नु
g: の can replace a previously mentioned noun. Nでよければ means “if N is acceptable.” Vちゃった is conversational Vてしまった.

p: あまり時間がないから、食事を（　）、簡単なものにするつもりだ。
en: Since I do not have much time, even if I eat, I intend to have something simple.
np: धेरै समय नभएकाले खाना खाए पनि सामान्य खाना खाने योजना छ।
why: Vるとしても means “even if one does V” or “even assuming V happens.”
wrong: するとしては does not express concession. するとしようと is incomplete. するとしようなら is not the correct conditional form; するとしたら would be grammatical.
v: 時間（じかん）= time / समय; 食事（しょくじ）= meal / खाना; 簡単な（かんたんな）= simple / सामान्य; つもり = intention / योजना
g: Vるとしても means “even if V.” Vるつもりだ expresses an intention.

p: 私はアイスクリームが大好きなので、お店で見かけると（　）。
o: 買わないでいられます
買わないではいられません
en: I love ice cream, so whenever I see it in a shop, I cannot help buying it.
np: मलाई आइसक्रिम धेरै मन पर्ने भएकाले पसलमा देख्दा नकिनी बस्न सक्दिनँ।
why: Vないではいられない means “cannot help doing” or “cannot refrain from doing.”
wrong: 買おうとしています means “am trying/about to buy.” 買おうとはしません means “do not try to buy.” 買わないでいられます means “can remain without buying,” the opposite meaning.
v: 私（わたし）= I / म; 大好き（だいすき）= love very much / धेरै मन पर्ने; 店（みせ）= shop / पसल; 見かける（みかける）= happen to see / देख्नु; 買う（かう）= buy / किन्नु
g: Vないではいられない means “cannot help doing V.” Vると expresses an automatic or repeated result.
